newsitem.title: USA: US envoy says China has long way to go on WTO bid.
newsitem.headline: US envoy says China has long way to go on WTO bid.

text.p: U.S. Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat said Wednesday that Beijing has a long way to go in its bid to join the World Trade Organization even though progress was made during recent talks in Geneva.
Eizenstat just returned to Washington from a trip to China that took him to Beijing, Shanghai and Hong Kong.

China's bid to enter the WTO was part of the discussions, Eizenstat said. Talks on China's WTO bid were going on in Geneva during Eizenstat's trip, during which he helped lay the groundwork for a visit by Vice President Al Gore later this month.
Eizenstat said progress was made during the talks, but that "we are still a long way from being at a point where accession is likely."
He said he talked to senior officials in Beijing about the huge U.S. trade deficit with China and the "corrosive" effect it could have on relations if not addressed.
Eizenstat said he told Chinese officials that the deficit was not sustainable and was a major problem for Congress.
"I got a clear sense that China was more sensitive to the issue of the growing deficit, to the impact it had in Washington," Eizenstat said.

Officials in China appeared willing to avoid what has been a frequent fight between Washington and Beijing over the size of the deficit and understand of the need to reduce barriers and increase market access, he said.
"Whether that will be translated into anything concrete, only time will tell," he told reporters.

Eizenstat said he told Beijing the best way to deal with the nearly $40 billion trade imbalance was to provide more open access to its markets and to allow U.S. companies a "fair opportunity" to win contracts in some of the huge infrastructure projects being planned in China.

Part of Eizenstat's visit was devoted to pushing for contracts on behalf of U.S. companies. Eizenstat declined to say how successful that effort was. Any announcements of successful contract bids would likely be made during Gore's trip.
